glossary.Inflammation: The body's protective response to injury or infection: redness, swelling, heat and pain.
glossary.Strep. pneumoniae: Pneumococcus: Gram-positive diplococcus, the commonest cause of community-acquired pneumonia.
glossary.S. aureus: Staphylococcus aureus: Gram-positive coccus causing skin, bone, blood and post-flu lung infections.
glossary.Pseudomonas: Gram-negative rod that causes hospital and ventilator infections and resists many antibiotics.
glossary.Klebsiella: Gram-negative rod causing severe pneumonia in alcohol misuse and diabetes.
glossary.H. influenzae: Haemophilus influenzae: Gram-negative coccobacillus linked with COPD exacerbations.
glossary.Intubation: Passing a breathing tube into the trachea, usually to ventilate a patient.
glossary.Infiltrate: Hazy shadowing on chest X-ray from fluid, cells or inflammation in the lung.
glossary.Multi-drug resistant: An organism resistant to several classes of antibiotics.
glossary.Gastric contents: Food, fluid and acid from the stomach.
glossary.Malnutrition: Poor nutritional state from too little or the wrong food.
glossary.NG feeding: Feeding through a nasogastric tube passed through the nose into the stomach.
glossary.Sputum: Mucus coughed up from the lower airways.
glossary.MCA stroke: Stroke in the middle cerebral artery territory, which can impair swallowing.
glossary.Cell wall: The rigid outer layer of bacteria; atypical organisms lack a typical one, so beta-lactams do not work.
glossary.Productive cough: A cough that brings up sputum.
glossary.Focal crackles: Crackles heard in one area of the chest.
glossary.COPD: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: long-term airflow limitation, usually from smoking.
glossary.Gram-negative rod: Rod-shaped bacterium staining pink on Gram stain.
glossary.Mycoplasma: Mycoplasma pneumoniae: an atypical bacterium with no cell wall, common in young adults.
glossary.Legionella: Legionella pneumophila: atypical bacterium spread through water systems such as air conditioning.
glossary.Bi-basal: Affecting the bases of both lungs.
glossary.Chlamydia psittaci: Atypical bacterium caught from birds, causing psittacosis.
glossary.HIV: Human immunodeficiency virus, which destroys CD4 T cells and causes immunodeficiency.
glossary.CT: Computed tomography: a cross-sectional X-ray scan.
glossary.Pleural fluid: Fluid collecting between the lung and chest wall.
glossary.Decreased breath sounds: Quieter breath sounds, heard over fluid, collapse or air.
glossary.Prognostic marker: A finding that predicts how a patient will do.
glossary.Confusion: New disorientation or reduced mental clarity.
glossary.Systolic: The higher blood pressure reading, during heart contraction.
glossary.Diastolic: The lower blood pressure reading, during heart relaxation.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: blood test of kidney function and salts.
glossary.SpO2: Oxygen saturation measured by a pulse oximeter.
glossary.EIA: Enzyme immunoassay: a lab test detecting an antigen or antibody.
glossary.Blood cultures: Blood samples incubated to grow and identify bacteria.
glossary.ABC: Airway, Breathing, Circulation: the order to assess and treat an unwell patient.
glossary.Amoxicillin: Oral penicillin antibiotic, first-line for low-severity CAP.
glossary.Doxycycline: Tetracycline antibiotic, an alternative in penicillin allergy.
glossary.Penicillin allergic: Having had a hypersensitivity reaction to penicillin antibiotics.
glossary.Septic: Having sepsis: life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the response to infection.
glossary.High-dependency setting: A unit with closer monitoring than a ward but less than ICU (HDU).
glossary.Meropenem: Broad-spectrum carbapenem antibiotic kept for severe or resistant infections.
glossary.3rd-gen cephalosporin: Broad-spectrum beta-lactam antibiotic such as ceftriaxone.
glossary.MRSA cover: Adding an antibiotic active against methicillin-resistant Staph. aureus.
glossary.Statins: Cholesterol-lowering drugs; levels rise with clarithromycin.
glossary.Plasma levels: Concentration of a drug in the blood.
glossary.Corticosteroids: Anti-inflammatory steroid drugs such as prednisolone.
glossary.COPD exacerbation: A flare of COPD with worse breathlessness, cough and sputum.
glossary.Lung parenchyma: The functional gas-exchanging tissue of the lung.
glossary.Exudate: Protein- and cell-rich fluid leaking from inflamed vessels.
glossary.Alveoli: Tiny air sacs where gas exchange happens.
glossary.Gas exchange: Movement of oxygen into and carbon dioxide out of the blood in the alveoli.
glossary.Neutrophilic: Driven by neutrophils, the white cells that fight bacteria.
glossary.Right main bronchus: The airway to the right lung; wider and more vertical than the left.
glossary.Flora: The mix of microbes normally living at a body site.
glossary.Decompensation: Failure of the body's compensatory mechanisms, so the illness becomes unstable.
glossary.Frailty: Reduced physiological reserve making a person vulnerable to illness.
